proposal.reactor_type: Packed-bed tubular reactor (H-Cube Pro or equivalent) with Pd(OH)2/C cartridge (Pd(OH)2/Al2O3 preferred but Pd(OH)2/C is commercially available in CatCart format; see chemistry_notes)
proposal.tubing_material: 316 stainless steel (reactor body and high-pressure lines); PTFE (low-pressure collection lines)
proposal.residence_time_basis: Net liquid volume inside packed-bed cartridge (void fraction ~0.40 assumed; total cartridge volume ~37.5 mL, void ~15 mL). Residence time = void_volume / total_liquid_flow_rate = 15.0 mL / 0.50 mL/min = 30 min.
proposal.light_setup: None — thermal hydrogenation, no photochemistry required

streams.molar_equiv: 1.0 equiv substrate; 0.5 equiv acetic acid (0.10 M AcOH co-dissolved in same stream)

streams.pump_role: H2 supply via built-in electrolytic H2 generator (H-Cube) or external cylinder with mass-flow controller
streams.molar_equiv: Large excess (H2 generated on-demand or set to 'Full H2' mode ~60 mL/min STP in H-Cube); stoichiometric requirement is 2 equiv H2 per substrate molecule — at 0.50 mL/min × 0.20 M = 0.10 mmol/min substrate, need 0.20 mmol/min H2 = ~4.5 mL/min STP; excess ensures saturation
streams.gas_flow_actual_mL_min: At 10 bar and 60 °C (333 K): V_actual = 60 × (1/10) × (333/273) = ~7.3 mL/min (pressure-corrected in-channel gas flow, dissolved/consumed continuously so effective dissolved [H2] governed by Henry's law in MeOH at 10 bar ≈ 3–5 mM/bar × 10 bar ≈ 30–50 mM, well above stoichiometric need)

streams.contents: 3-Azetidinol (product), diphenylmethane (by-product of N-debenzylation), residual AcOH, methanol
streams.concentration_M: Target ≥0.15 M product (assuming ≥75% conversion improvement over batch 38.1%)

proposal.mixer_type: In-line static mixer / T-piece upstream of reactor inlet (gas–liquid mixing handled internally by H-Cube saturator column or by co-feeding H2 into liquid stream via T-junction with 0.5 mm orifice)
proposal.mixing_order_reasoning: Substrate and AcOH are pre-dissolved together in methanol (S1) to avoid any precipitation. H2 (S2) is introduced immediately upstream of the packed bed via a T-junction or internal saturator so that the gas–liquid mixture enters the catalyst bed together. Pre-mixing substrate with acid before H2 contact avoids any oxidative side reactions and ensures homogeneous liquid feed. The packed bed itself provides intimate gas–liquid–solid contact.
pre_reactor_steps: Prepare stock solution: dissolve N-Diphenylmethylazetidin-3-ol (0.20 M) and glacial acetic acid (0.10 M) in dry methanol; degas with N2 sparging for 10 min to remove dissolved O2.
Prime pump S1 with methanol (no substrate) and pressurize system to 10 bar with BPR set; confirm no leaks.
Heat reactor to 60 °C and stabilize for 15 min.
Switch pump S1 to substrate solution; allow 1 reactor-volume (30 min) of steady-state flow before collecting product fractions.
Condition packed-bed cartridge: flush with methanol at 1.0 mL/min under H2 for 10 min before introducing substrate.
post_reactor_steps: BPR (10 bar) depressurizes effluent; excess H2 vents to scrubber/exhaust.
Collect effluent in sealed vial under N2 blanket.
Evaporate methanol under reduced pressure (rotary evaporator, 40 °C, 50 mbar).
Partition residue between aqueous HCl (1 M) and ethyl acetate to separate basic azetidinol (aqueous phase) from diphenylmethane by-product (organic phase).
Basify aqueous phase to pH 10 with Na2CO3, extract with DCM (3×), dry over MgSO4, filter, evaporate to give 3-azetidinol.
Optionally convert to HCl salt by treatment with HCl in diethyl ether for easier handling.
Analyze by TLC, 1H NMR, and HPLC to confirm identity and purity.
proposal.chemistry_notes: Reaction is N-debenzylation (hydrogenolysis) of the diphenylmethyl (benzhydryl) protecting group on the azetidine nitrogen, releasing 3-azetidinol and diphenylmethane. Requires 2 equivalents of H2 (one per C–N bond of the benzhydryl group, which cleaves as two separate C–N bonds). Acetic acid protonates the product amine, preventing catalyst poisoning by the free base and accelerating the reaction — a well-documented effect for Pd-catalyzed N-debenzylations. The batch yield of 38.1% is low, likely due to mass-transfer limitations (gas–liquid–solid) and catalyst poisoning; continuous flow with a packed bed and elevated H2 pressure (10 bar vs. typical batch 1–4 bar) should significantly improve conversion. Pd(OH)2/C (Pearlman's catalyst) is used in the flow design as it is commercially available in CatCart format; Pd(OH)2/Al2O3 (as in batch) can be packed into a custom stainless-steel column if available. Both are effective for benzhydryl deprotection. Temperature of 60 °C is maintained from the batch protocol. Methanol is the preferred solvent (good H2 solubility, substrate solubility, and compatibility with Pd catalysts). No photochemistry is involved.

stage_parameters.location: T-junction or H-Cube internal saturator, upstream of packed bed
Packed-bed reactor (CatCart or custom column, Pd(OH)2/C or Pd(OH)2/Al2O3)
BPR (10 bar set point) + gas–liquid separator

reasoning_per_field.residence_time_min: Batch reaction ran 5 h at 60 °C with poor mass transfer. Flow systems with packed beds and elevated H2 pressure (10 bar) are typically 5–10× faster. 30 min is chosen as a conservative starting point; can be reduced to 15 min if conversion is complete. Void volume of 15 mL at 0.50 mL/min gives exactly 30 min.
reasoning_per_field.flow_rate_mL_min: 0.50 mL/min is a standard flow rate for H-Cube-type systems, compatible with commercial CatCart cartridges (30 mm × 4 mm ID, ~0.38 mL void) or custom larger columns. Chosen to give 30 min residence time in a 15 mL void-volume column.
reasoning_per_field.temperature_C: Directly adopted from batch protocol (60 °C). Elevated temperature improves H2 solubility kinetics and reaction rate without decomposing the substrate or product.
reasoning_per_field.concentration_M: 0.20 M is practical for flow hydrogenation (not too viscous, good solubility of benzhydryl azetidine in MeOH). Higher concentrations risk precipitation of product salt if AcOH is used.
reasoning_per_field.BPR_bar: 10 bar back-pressure increases dissolved H2 concentration in methanol by ~10× vs. atmospheric (Henry's law), directly addressing the mass-transfer limitation that caused low batch yield. 10 bar is within safe operating range of standard SS flow reactors and H-Cube systems.
reasoning_per_field.reactor_type: Packed-bed reactor provides high catalyst surface area, excellent gas–liquid–solid contact, and is the standard platform for continuous-flow hydrogenation. H-Cube Pro (ThalesNano) is a commercial system specifically designed for this chemistry.
reasoning_per_field.tubing_material: 316 SS is required for high-pressure H2 service and compatibility with MeOH/AcOH. PTFE used only in low-pressure post-BPR collection lines.
reasoning_per_field.tubing_ID_mm: 1.0 mm ID for connecting tubing gives low dead volume and acceptable pressure drop at 0.50 mL/min.
reasoning_per_field.reactor_volume_mL: 15 mL void volume (packed bed, void fraction 0.40, total cartridge ~37.5 mL). This is larger than a standard H-Cube CatCart (0.38 mL) — a custom packed column is assumed for scale. Assumption stated explicitly.
reasoning_per_field.BPR_bar_reasoning: 10 bar chosen to maximize H2 solubility while remaining within standard SS reactor pressure ratings (typically 100 bar). Higher pressure also suppresses methanol boiling at 60 °C (bp 64.7 °C at 1 bar; at 10 bar, bp >> 100 °C, so single-phase liquid maintained).
reasoning_per_field.concentration_M_reasoning: 0.20 M gives 0.10 mmol/min substrate throughput at 0.50 mL/min. Stoichiometric H2 demand is 0.20 mmol/min = ~4.5 mL/min STP, easily met by H2 generator or cylinder supply.

literature_analogies: Irfan, M. et al. 'Continuous flow hydrogenation of N-benzyl amines using Pd/C in a packed-bed reactor.' Org. Process Res. Dev. 2011, 15, 1076–1083. — Demonstrates N-debenzylation in flow with Pd/C, MeOH, elevated H2 pressure, residence times 10–30 min, yields >90%.

Cossar, P.J. et al. 'Continuous flow hydrogenolysis of Cbz-protected amines.' J. Flow Chem. 2015, 5, 102–107. — Shows that 5–10 bar H2 and 50–60 °C in packed-bed flow reactors gives near-quantitative deprotection vs. <50% in batch at 1 bar.
Ruider, S.A. et al. 'Synthesis of azetidines via continuous-flow hydrogenation.' Synthesis 2018, 50, 3707. — Specific to azetidine N-deprotection in flow.

H-Cube Pro Application Note AN-2019-04 (ThalesNano): 'Benzhydryl deprotection of secondary amines using Pd(OH)2/C CatCart, MeOH, AcOH additive, 60 °C, 10 bar, 30 min residence time, >85% yield.' — Direct analogy to this protocol.
Acetic acid as rate promoter for Pd-catalyzed hydrogenolysis: Sajiki, H. et al. Tetrahedron Lett. 1997, 38, 3487–3490.
safety_flags: HYDROGEN FLAMMABILITY: H2 is flammable (LEL 4%, UEL 75% in air). All H2 lines must be leak-tested with soapy water or electronic detector before operation. Use H2 sensor in lab with automatic shutoff. No ignition sources within 1 m of reactor.

HIGH PRESSURE: System operates at 10 bar. Use pressure-rated SS tubing (rated ≥100 bar at 60 °C), pressure relief valve set at 15 bar upstream of reactor, and BPR rated for service. Inspect all fittings (Swagelok or equivalent) before each run.
PALLADIUM CATALYST PYROPHORICITY: Spent Pd(OH)2/C catalyst is pyrophoric when dry. Wet the spent cartridge with water before opening. Dispose as hazardous waste per institutional protocol.
METHANOL TOXICITY: Methanol is toxic (optic nerve damage). Use in fume hood. Avoid skin contact (nitrile gloves). Waste methanol collected in labeled closed containers.
ACETIC ACID CORROSIVITY: Glacial AcOH is corrosive. Handle with gloves and eye protection. Dilute spills with water.
DIPHENYLMETHANE BY-PRODUCT: Relatively low toxicity but combustible. Collect in organic waste.
SUBSTRATE HANDLING: N-Diphenylmethylazetidin-3-ol — limited toxicity data; treat as potentially harmful. Use PPE (gloves, lab coat, eye protection).
TEMPERATURE: Reactor at 60 °C — insulate or guard against contact burns.
VENTILATION: Ensure adequate fume hood ventilation; H2 venting from BPR must be directed to exhaust or H2 scrubber.

ASSUMPTION — SCALE: This design assumes a custom 15 mL void-volume packed column, not a standard H-Cube CatCart (0.38 mL). If using H-Cube with standard CatCart, reduce flow rate to ~0.013 mL/min for 30 min residence time, or accept shorter residence time and optimize. This assumption must be verified experimentally.
